we have synthesized a new phosphine‐oxide‐based sulfonated poly(amic acid) (S‐BAPPO‐PA) and its corresponding polyimide (S‐BapPO‐PI), that we have characterized their thermal behavior, and that we have studied their proton conductivities.
we synthesized a novel phosphine oxide-containing sulfonated polyamide monomer, which was used in the synthesis of new sulfonated poly(imide-co-amine)s.

the synthesis of new polyimide membranes with good proton conductivity.
the development of novel sulfonated poly(amic acid)s and polyimides with good proton conductivity and thermal stability for use as proton exchange membranes.
the synthesis and characterization of novel phosphorus-containing sulfonated poly(ether imide)s.

the phosphine oxide-based polyimide membrane has a good potential for use as a proton exchange membrane in fuel cells.
the novel phosphine oxide-based polyimide is an attractive candidate for the preparation of proton exchange membranes.
the novel BAPPO-based sulfonated polymers are promising proton exchange membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sulfonated BAPPPO monomer is a promising candidate for use in the synthesis for proton exchange membranes, and the resulting polyimide has good proton conductivity, good thermal stability, and good mechanical properties.

sulfonated phosphine oxide-based polyimides have a high potential as proton exchange membranes for fuel cells, and that the sulfonated monomer 1,4-bis(4-aminophenoxy)benzene 2-phenyl-2-phosphonic acid (BAPPO) is a very good monomer for the synthesis of sulfonated poly(amic acids) and polyimides.
we have developed an efficient method of synthesizing a new sulfonated poly(amic acid) precursor and a new phosphorus-containing polyimide membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phosphine oxide group in the polyimides is not detrimental to proton conductivity and that the polyimides have a high thermal stability and a good proton conductivity.
phosphorus-containing sulfonated poly(amic acid)s can be used as proton conductors in fuel cells.
the phosphine oxide group can be used as a new sulfonatable moiety in polyimide synthesis and that the resulting polyimides are suitable as proton exchange membranes.
